title: Evaluation of coherent isomorphisms in a Segal space
statement:
Use spaces, simplicial sets, nerves and coherent mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Put $\mathcal P_\Delta=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. For a simplicial set $K$, let $dK$ be the simplicial space with discrete values $K_n$. Let $W\in\mathcal P_\Delta$ be a Segal space, meaning that $W_n\to W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$ is an equivalence for every $n\geq2$. Its mapping space $W(x,y)$ is the homotopy fiber of $(d_1,d_0):W_1\to W_0^2$ over $(x,y)$. Let $hW$ have objects the points of $W_0$ and morphisms $\pi_0W(x,y)$, with composition induced by the Segal maps and identities by $s_0$. Let $W_{\mathrm{inv}}\subset W_1$ be the union of components consisting of arrows invertible in $hW$. Let $J$ be the ordinary category with two objects $0,1$ and one morphism between every ordered pair, and put $E=N(J)$. Evaluation at its edge $0\to1$ induces a natural equivalence of spaces over $W_0^2$
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P_\Delta}(dE,W)\xrightarrow{\simeq}W_{\mathrm{inv}}.$$
Consequently its homotopy fiber over $(x,y)$ is the union of invertible components of $W(x,y)$. No completeness condition on $W$ is assumed.

source.place: Sections 5.5 and 5.7, Lemma 5.8, Theorem 6.2 and its proof in Section 11 (in particular Proposition 11.1). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Work with bisimplicial sets, with Kan model structure in the inner direction. The Reedy structure exists by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], applied to each row of fixed inner degree, the latching object consists exactly of the outer-degenerate simplices. Indeed, two degeneracy presentations are identified in the latching colimit through the unique nondegenerate presentation. For a monomorphism A→B the relative latching map therefore identifies with the inclusion A_n∪L_nB→B_n: if a degeneracy of B lies in A, a section of its degeneracy operator recovers its preimage in A. Thus Reedy cofibrations are precisely the monomorphisms, and every bisimplicial set, in particular dE and F(n)=dΔ^n, is Reedy cofibrant. The objectwise tensor and cotensor give the usual simplicial enrichment. To check its model axiom, the relative latching map of i□j is (A_n∪_{L_nA}L_nB→B_n)□j. The Cartesian simplicial Kan model axiom supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] makes this a (trivial) cofibration if i,j are cofibrations and either is trivial; when i is trivial its relative latching maps are trivial by the Reedy theorem. This verifies the simplicial model structure needed below without applying the complete-Segal-space localization.

source.place: Agent model comparison, step 1; Rezk §2.4–2.5; Stacks Tag 017R for the latching calculation.

proof.text: Apply the unlocalized comparison in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison] with the small ordinary category D=Δ. It identifies objectwise localization of simplicial presheaves with P_Δ and retains coherent transformations and mapping spaces. Represent W by a strict simplicial diagram X and use the functorial Reedy factorization X→V→* of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], with X→V an objectwise weak equivalence and V Reedy fibrant. Then V still represents W. Its matching fibrations give Kan V_0 and V_1→V_0², hence fibrations V_1→V_0 at either endpoint. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], ordinary composable-edge fiber products of V_1 compute their homotopy fiber products. The Segal condition on W therefore says exactly that V_n→V_1×_{V_0}⋯×_{V_0}V_1 is a weak equivalence. Thus V satisfies the Reedy fibrant Segal-space hypotheses of the existing classifier, without requiring completeness.

source.place: Agent model comparison, step 2; Rezk §4 Segal condition and the unlocalized simplicial-presheaf comparison.

proof.text: The Reedy weak equivalences are objectwise, so its coherent localization is the same localization used in step 2. Since dE and every F(n) are cofibrant and V is fibrant, [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies their enriched mapping simplicial sets with the mapping spaces in P_Δ. In particular Map_{P_Δ}(dE,W) is represented by the Kan complex whose q-simplices are natural maps dE×cΔ^q→V. Here c denotes the constant outer diagram. This is exactly (V^{dE})_0 with the internal-hom convention of [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-classifier]. For F(n), a natural map F(n)×cΔ^q→V is determined by its value at id_[n], with inverse taking a simplex v to its restrictions V(α)v for α:[k]→[n]; thus the enriched mapping complex is V_n. These identifications respect restriction along the edge F(1)→dE and the two vertices F(0)→dE, because both operations are precomposition.

source.place: Agent model comparison, step 3; Rezk §2.3 for internal mapping objects, and coherent simplicial-model localization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-classifier] to V. Its groupoid I[1] is precisely the category J in the item, so its discrete nerve is dE here. It gives the natural weak equivalence ε_V:(V^{dE})_0→V_eq induced by the distinguished edge 0→1, and explicitly makes this a map over V_0² whose endpoint maps are the two vertex restrictions. Thus the actual evaluation map of step 3, rather than an unspecified equivalence between its source and target spaces, identifies its source with V_eq.

source.place: Agent reuse of the existing classifier; Rezk Theorem 6.2 and §11. This is an existing DAG node, not a new restatement.

proof.text: Under the presentation V≃W the degree-zero and degree-one spaces and their endpoint maps are identified. Taking homotopy fibers therefore identifies the mapping spaces of V and W at corresponding endpoints. The degree-two maps and s_0 identify composition and identity classes: a class represented by f has an inverse if and only if there is a reverse class g with [gf]=[s_0x] and [fg]=[s_0y], and these two equations are preserved and reflected by these identifications. Consequently V_eq identifies exactly with W_inv. Substitute these identifications and the comparison of step 3 into ε_V to obtain Map_{P_Δ}(dE,W)≃W_inv over W_0². This is natural in W: the classifier is natural, and [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison] retains coherent transformations, while the mapping-space comparison respects compositions. Independently of the presentation, the map so identified is the original restriction along 0→1.

source.place: Agent model comparison, step 5: transport the evaluation map and its endpoint maps, not just its homotopy type.

proof.text: Pull back the equivalence over W_0² along (x,y). Pullback of an equivalence is an equivalence, since pulling back its inverse and inverse homotopies gives inverse maps. The right-hand pullback is the subspace of W(x,y) whose projected edge belongs to W_inv. This condition is constant on each component and, by the definition of W_inv and of hW, holds exactly when that morphism class is invertible. This proves the stated fiber description. Only the Segal condition and Reedy replacement were used; no completeness hypothesis entered.

source.place: Agent model comparison, step 6: homotopy pullback of the resulting equivalence and the definitions in the item.
